experiment: The retry path on real damage: a copy of Omikron - The Nomad Soul scratched through the label side, with material missing from the data layer in tracks 1 and 2. The console still boots it (it boots from track 3).
observed: Setup: FAD 8345 (last sector of audio track 2) failed twice with sense 3/2 (medium error), then read on the third attempt
Capture, track 1: the opening 32-sector PIO read at FAD 150 failed; single-sector recovery read FAD 150 on its first retry and committed it
FAD 151 failed all 10 retries with sense 3/2: 'Read retries exhausted: track 01 FAD=151'
CAPTURE/VERIFY FAILED: last committed bytes=2352; retries=13 / Partial job preserved
the capture phase took 5.0 s; no hang (each failed read is bounded)

conclusions: The retry path works on real media: a failed multi-sector read drops to single-sector reads, which pinned the damage to the exact sector (FAD 151) and kept the good sector before it.

It gives up after a fixed 10 retries (11 attempts, the same bound the host tests assert), names the sector, keeps the partial job and stops cleanly. It never zero-fills or skips, so no dump is ever produced with a sector that was not read.

The failing reads were the track's opening PIO chunk (CMD 16), not DMA, so the DMA stop flaw fixed in v6.2 was not involved; with the damage mid-track, v6.2 logs 'GD-ROM DMA read failed ... re-reading this chunk with PIO' first.
The disc cannot be dumped by any drive: the data layer is physically gone. The same title's good copy was dumped and verified separately (lid-open-omikron-2026-09-20.json).

note: This copy gets a different disc identity from the good one (8cd1c022... against def8ea0e...), so its partial job is kept apart and cannot be resumed into the good copy's job.
